questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience and explore the world, while challenging myself to live and work in a new environment

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to study in Sydney because i wanted to study near a bigger city with lots of opportunities for unique experiences, but also stay within an English speaking country. I also wanted to be close to beautiful nature and citylife

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I absolutely loved going abroad, but felt that the teaching did not meet the high standards of UCPH. The uni itself is nice, but I felt it was a bit too easy. I also had the majority of my teaching done via zoom or prerecorded lectures. It did however give me a lot of freedom to meet up with friends and to travel. WSU's disability services are quite good and they offer lots of help

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Orientation was pretty good and I received pamphlets regarding the uni/teaching itself, sports clubs (they only had a few), disability services etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I contacted disability services prior to arriving at the uni, so later upon arrival I already had a scheduled meeting with them and they could assist me in putting together my academic integration plan and tell me about how their semester works

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I stayed at the student accommodation village. It is a bunch of apartments within a gated community. You can choose apartments of different sized, with different amounts of roommates

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Each apartment has a full size kitchen, although you have to buy plates, pans etc. yourself. A couple times a month a chaplaincy came to the village and served a meal. Another group served dinner on campus a couple times a month.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit noisy, but the student accommodation is quite nice. Since the uni mainly has foreign students, you will most likely not live with any Australian roomies, which I personally would have liked to do. Be prepared for cultural differences when living with people from all over the world

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Sometimes the village scheduled events, movie nights or other things to get to know your fellow students

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up for the courses via the uni's online course registration page. I had some issues registering for all of my courses, but I contacted student services and they signed me up manually. After signing up for the courses I was able to apply for which of the multiple classes I wanted to join, depending on my preferred timetable

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student services are able to help with registration

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to get all of the courses I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Contact student services if you have any issues

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took both first and third year courses, since I had some restricted electives and some non-restricted electives. All of the courses were very easy and I was able to get pretty good grades without studying or doing my best on the tests and assignments. Don't expect to be academically challenged

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was pretty different. I didn't have any lectures in a big auditorium, but instead had all of my lectures online. Most of my classes were also online, although some of my friends from other faculties had most of their classes in person. The lecturers seemed pretty knowledgeable. Some courses' tutorials were taught by the lecturers, other tutorials were taught by phD students, who weren't equipped to be teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Advanced physiology
Molecular medicine
Psychology: Behavioral science
Contextualising indigenous Australia (Day mode)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend 'Contextualising indigenous Australia (Day mode)'. Although it was a pretty easy course and at times a bit boring, it offered me great knowledge about the history of Australia and it's native people. It offered some perspective on the current situation in Australia, where the existence of Aboriginals still is an important topic

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Alcohol is very expensive, so going out can eat up quite a bit of your budget

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is more expensive than I expected. Be wise about grocery shopping, then you can save a bit of money

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many different societies for different ethnicities. There were also some social clubs and sports clubs, however the clubs were run by students, so the clubs I joined unfortunately didn't host any events in the time I was there. The dinners or events hosted by the uni were great though

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would join the chaplaincy dinners hosted by the uni and would join in on the sports clubs and events that do host events and competitions. I also highly recommend joining the activities hosted by the student village

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: During the semester I visited Bali, Melbourne and Tasmania, and I highly recommend all of those places! But in Sydney there is also plenty to do! I really enjoyed going to the Blue Mountains, Sydney Harbour, touring the Opera House or the many free museums and galleries in Sydney as well as Taronga Zoo

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, there isn't really any major cultural differences except the fact that Australians generally are more welcoming and talkative towards strangers than Danes are

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Unfortunately not, as there aren't many Australian students at WSU

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved how open and welcoming Australians are

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't expect a high academic level, go traveling as well as exploring Sydney as much as you possibly can since this uni offers a lot of freedom and utilize the many social opportunities at both the uni itself and the student village

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You do not need to buy the books. Either you can do completely without reading or you can find some of the books online for free. Also be aware that the uni itself is located outside of downtown Sydney, with at least 35-60 minutes of travel to downtown or the beaches

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to explore lovely Sydney and making friends while doing it

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me personally it was challenging to establish a new everyday life, and starting over at a new uni that does things differently than UCPH. You will also have to learn to deal with FOMO as you will never be able to experience everything that all the other students are doing

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
